justification_text:
My point estimates across the three horizons reflect a modest upward drift from what I assessed as the prevailing price level near 31.25. At the one-day horizon, the estimate stays essentially anchored to current conditions, as overnight price movement in most assets tends to be small relative to the broader trend, and I saw no immediate catalysts strong enough to force a sharp departure. Moving out to one week, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to 31.40, reflecting a gentle continuation of whatever near-term momentum or fundamental support appeared to be present. At one month, I moved to 31.80, acknowledging that slightly longer time horizons allow for more drift in the direction of any underlying trend, while still keeping the estimate relatively conservative given the uncertainty that compounds over time.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to reflect how uncertainty naturally expands as the forecast horizon lengthens. At one day, the interval is quite tight — just one full point wide — because short-term price behavior in liquid markets tends to be mean-reverting around recent levels and large single-day moves are relatively rare absent a specific shock. By one week, the interval widens to nearly four points, capturing the possibility of several trading sessions worth of accumulating volatility, news flow, or sentiment shifts. At one month, the interval expands further to roughly 8.5 points, reflecting the reality that over a four-week window, macroeconomic data releases, policy announcements, and shifts in market positioning can all compound in ways that are genuinely difficult to anticipate.

There are meaningful risks that could push realized outcomes outside even these widened intervals. On the upside, an unexpected positive catalyst — such as a stronger-than-anticipated economic data print, a bullish policy surprise, or a sudden shift in institutional demand — could drive prices well above 36 at the monthly horizon. On the downside, a risk-off episode triggered by geopolitical escalation, a financial stress event, or a sharp repricing of interest rate expectations could easily break below 27.50. Liquidity conditions also matter: if trading becomes thin around major holidays or event dates, price moves can be amplified beyond what historical volatility alone would suggest. These tail scenarios are real, even if my stated intervals are intended to cover the central 90 percent of plausible outcomes.
